## Independent continuation: arbitrary panel and exact defect

For endpoints a<b let h=b−a. The line joining (a,a²) and (b,b²) is L(x)=(a+b)x−ab. Hence

L(x)−x²=(x−a)(b−x).

This polynomial identity can be checked directly and vanishes at both endpoints. Its integral is h³/6, since substitution x=a+ht gives h³∫₀¹t(1−t)dt=h³/6. For any increasing partition 0=x₀<…<x_n=1 with h_i=x_i−x_{i−1}, additivity gives the exact signed error

T−I=(1/6)Σ_i h_i³>0,     I=1/3.

Uniform widths h_i=1/n yield T_n−I=1/(6n²), independently confirming the inherited result. This is an identity for every positive integer n under exact arithmetic, not a finite-data fit.

## Equal spacing uniquely minimizes error for fixed panel count

Set m=1/n. For every positive h the identity

h³−m³−3m²(h−m)=(h−m)²(h+2m)

has a nonnegative right side. Sum it over the widths. Because Σ_i(h_i−m)=0 and nm³=1/n²,

Σ_i h_i³−1/n²=Σ_i(h_i−m)²(h_i+2m)≥0.

Consequently

T−I=1/(6n²)+(1/6)Σ_i(h_i−1/n)²(h_i+2/n).

Every coefficient h_i+2/n is positive, so equality occurs exactly when all widths equal 1/n. This proves that uniform spacing uniquely minimizes trapezoidal error for x² among partitions with the same positive panel count. It also quantifies the excess due to unequal widths without appealing to a general convexity theorem.

For example, two widths 1/4 and 3/4 give error ((1/4)³+(3/4)³)/6=7/96, exceeding the uniform two-panel error 1/24=4/96. These are hand-derived rational values, not executed numerical output.

Bisecting a width h replaces h³/6 by 2(h/2)³/6=h³/24. Thus bisecting every panel quarters total error even for a nonuniform original partition. For one bisected panel the error reduction is h³/8. Let H=max_i h_i. Since h_i³≤H²h_i and Σ_i h_i=1, the exact formula implies 0<T−I≤H²/6. A mesh sequence with H tending to zero therefore converges; the number of panels alone does not enforce convergence for arbitrary nonuniform partitions unless widths also shrink.

For uniform refinement the exact cancellation (4T_{2n}−T_n)/3=1/3 follows by substitution. On each pair of half-panels that expression has weights h/6 at the endpoints and 2h/3 at the midpoint, explaining its exactness on this quadratic directly from the previously proved panel errors.

On a panel of width h centered at m, write x=m+t with -h/2<=t<=h/2. Its trapezoidal contribution is

h[(m-h/2)^2+(m+h/2)^2]/2 = h m^2+h^3/4.

integral_{-h/2}^{h/2}(m+t)^2 dt = h m^2+h^3/12,

T_n - integral_0^1 x^2 dx = n h^3/6 = 1/(6n^2),

and hence T_n=1/3+1/(6n^2). This centered-panel argument verifies that the coefficient is independent of panel location and agrees with both predecessor proofs. It is an exact algebraic calculation for arbitrary positive integer n, not a fit to selected values. Reversing the error convention reverses the sign.

The result implies 4 T_{2n}-T_n=1, so (4 T_{2n}-T_n)/3=1/3 exactly in exact arithmetic.
